answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused a price reopening, making renewal unlikely to meet the mandated 18% spend reduction. The previously low-cost vendor is the only inherited option with evidence of sharp unit-cost savings and quick onboarding, while the incumbent record provides the delivery-stability baseline that must be protected during transition. Because the contract ends in 14 days and the line has no volume buffer, switching must include explicit continuity controls; archived records should be checked for any delivery-performance limits or transition caveats before commitment.
